_comment: Human skin, Fitzpatrick type III (Phase07 step 7.1). SUBSURFACE: skin's look is light scattering inside it. Topology-free (CM2): a tone plus a tiling micro-surface at real size, so it works on any mesh. Values from Physically Based `Skin III` (albedo, IOR 1.4, roughness 0.5, scatter distance). `subsurface_radius` is in metres (OpenPBR scene units; Learnings/MaterialX M4): Physically Based gives the diffuse mean free path in cm (0.482, 0.169, 0.109), so 4.82 mm red, with the channels over it as the scale. `subsurface_weight` 1.0 and `subsurface_color` = the albedo (judgement): skin is a scattering body throughout, and OpenPBR mixes the diffuse colour towards `subsurface_color` by the weight, so an unset colour (OpenPBR's light grey) would wash the tone out. The shared `Skin_Pores` micro-surface (pores and furrows at a 1 cm tile) is the article's OWN normal and roughness, not a wear overlay: an overlay ships at 0 (C1) and would leave the skin plastic by default. Wear layers at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage) and dust/dirt (overlay 2).
name: Skin_FitzpatrickIII_Clean_Base_s001_v01

sources.note: roughness 0.5 is the MEAN of the Skin_Pores roughness map

sources.why: subsurface_weight 1.0 and subsurface_color = the albedo: skin scatters throughout, and OpenPBR's default subsurface colour (light grey) would desaturate the tone.
